criteria.mastery_indicator: Student describes polarization from the electric field vector's direction and motion.
common_misconceptions: Polarization is the direction the whole wave object travels.
A larger field vector means a different propagation direction.

criteria.mastery_indicator: Student explains that a linear polarizer transmits the field component along its axis.
common_misconceptions: A linear polarizer rotates the incoming wave without reducing amplitude.
A crossed polarizer blocks light because the wave has stopped moving.

criteria.mastery_indicator: Student explains that a quarter-wave plate introduces a relative phase shift between orthogonal components.
common_misconceptions: A quarter-wave plate is the same as a second linear polarizer.
Circular polarization means the wave travels in a circle.
